subject.title: Exec allowlist matches never auto-execute on darwin — "allowlist auto-execution is unavailable on darwin; reviewer or explicit approval is required" (2026.6.11)

question: Should Darwin allowlist matches that require shell expansion or shell control syntax gain a narrower auto-execution path, or should OpenClaw keep prompting and improve documentation and diagnostics only?
rationale: The current gate is deliberately preventing auto-execution when the gateway cannot rebuild a command that pins resolved executables, and changing it affects when host exec bypasses human approval.

options.title: Keep fail-closed, improve diagnostics
options.body: Preserve the current prompt behavior for unenforceable shell-shaped commands and update docs/warnings to name the command-shape reason such as tilde, glob, pipe, or shell-wrapper payload.

options.title: Add narrow safe rewrites
options.body: Allow only audited shell-free rewrites for low-risk common forms such as tilde-expanded script paths, with tests proving no shell injection or trust drift.

options.title: Broaden auto-execution
options.body: Permit more shell-shaped allowlist matches to auto-run, accepting a larger security review and regression-proof burden.

recommendation.title: Keep fail-closed, improve diagnostics
recommendation.body: Preserve the current prompt behavior for unenforceable shell-shaped commands and update docs/warnings to name the command-shape reason such as tilde, glob, pipe, or shell-wrapper payload.

likelyOwner.reason: The current code and most relevant regression-history evidence point to vincentkoc as the best available owner for the exec approval boundary decision.
